What this website uses, how it uses it, and what is still missing.

Original API requests & regional snapshot files +
Research datasets planned for future integration +

NASA GPM IMERG ↗
Half-hourly precipitation at 0.1°. Not connected in this version. POWER PRECTOTCORR is not represented as IMERG.

NASA SMAP ↗
Satellite soil moisture. Not connected. Current soil values come from the explicitly labelled Open-Meteo weather model.

NASA GEOS-FP ↗
Atmospheric forecasts. Not connected. Future rain in this version comes from Open-Meteo.

NASA NASADEM ↗
Terrain and drainage analysis. Not connected. The current elevation comes from the Open-Meteo response.

NASA MODIS / VIIRS flood maps ↗
Observed surface water for future validation. Not ingested. Scenario flood zones are illustrative.

Mekong River Commission ↗
River-stage monitoring. No station feed is connected. Actual water level and rise rate remain unavailable.

NASA–ISRO NISAR ↗
SAR change detection. Not ingested. This prototype is not yet a validated submission for a NISAR-specific challenge.

How the index works

Understand the risk score.

Five factors contribute to a 0–100 educational screening index. The weights are chosen for this prototype; they have not been fitted or calibrated against Vietnamese flood events.

Future rainfall35%
Previous rainfall25%
Soil moisture20%
Low-elevation proxy10%
River rise rate10%
Vietnam Flood Watch

A student research prototype. Not a flood probability, official warning, or verified safe-route service.
AI-assisted interface and code. NASA does not endorse this project. Follow local authorities for travel and emergency decisions.

Vietnam official forecasts ↗
TRANSPARENT CALCULATION

What the number means.

This is an experimental screening score, not a probability of flooding. Every factor is scaled to 0–1 and then multiplied by its weight.

Future rain · 35%next 24h rain / 150 mm
Previous rain · 25%latest 3 complete NASA days / 300 mm
Soil moisture · 20%(volumetric moisture − 0.15) / 0.35
Low elevation · 10%1 − elevation / 50 m
River rise · 10%positive rise rate / 0.30 m per hour

Each scaled value is clamped to 0–1. Thresholds: Low <20; Watch 20–49; High 50–74; Very high ≥75. These are demonstration thresholds, not hydrological standards.

Missing data stays missing.

Without river observations, we show a score interval: the lower bound is the known contribution, and the upper bound includes the entire missing weight. We never assume the river is stable or call this a confidence interval. NASA rainfall may lag the weather forecast; their exact windows are shown.

Scale matters.

One reference point represents each study area. These are not district-wide forecasts. Absolute elevation does not capture drainage, tides, dam releases, blocked drains or flash-flood dynamics. Northern mountain scores are especially limited. Regional colours cannot determine whether a street is passable.

Local route scenarios

Route geometry, when available, follows OpenStreetMap roads via OSRM. Scenario comparison samples the route every ~20 m against illustrative flood circles and weights overlap by severity. A lower simulated exposure does not establish that a road is safe. The source-data view never ranks road safety.

Validation still required

Independent historical events, correct publication-time inputs, local rainfall and water-level observations, false-alarm and missed-event checks are needed before operational use.
